title: MGFs, Cumulants and Central Moments
breadcrumb: Probability → MGFs, cumulants and central moments
objectives: Define an MGF and identify its interval of existence around zero.
Obtain raw moments by differentiating the MGF at zero.
Use products and substitutions for independent sums and affine transformations.
Derive cumulants from the log-MGF and use additivity.
Convert raw moments, central moments and cumulants correctly.

prereq.name: Independence and sums of random variables

traps: An MGF must exist near zero for the usual uniqueness result.
Independent MGFs multiply; cumulant functions add.
For aX+b, κ_r=aʳκ_r(X) for r≥2; translation changes only κ₁.
The lognormal has no finite MGF for positive t.

sheet: Independent sums: MGFs multiply, cumulants add.
tricks: Take log M before differentiating cumulants.
shortcuts: Add independent cumulants order by order.
Normal cumulants above order two vanish.
remember: Raw moments are about zero; central moments are about μ.
The fourth cumulant is not the fourth central moment.

howto: Differentiate M for raw moments, but take its logarithm first for cumulants. Work the Poisson and binomial examples, then compare the fourth cumulant with the fourth central moment. Check the MGF existence condition.

scenes.title: Before the lesson — four foundations
body: An MGF stores raw moments; the cumulant function simplifies independent sums.
The distinction matters: M''(0) is a raw second moment, not a variance.

ask.nudge: It is not yet centred at the mean.

refresh: It is M'(0) when the MGF exists.
Subtract the squared mean from the raw second moment.

items.ask: What is the MGF of an independent sum?

items.recall: log M(t), the cumulant generating function.
refresh: Its derivatives at zero are cumulants.

scenes.title: Why the logarithm helps
body: An MGF stores moments in one function. Repeated differentiation can become algebraically messy.
For independent variables, the MGF of a sum is a product. Taking logarithms turns that product into a sum.
At orders three and four, central moments and cumulants no longer coincide.

scenario.teaser: A risk analyst needs the skewness of a total count from independent portfolios.
scenario.title: Cumulants turn convolution into addition
body: Two independent claim-count portfolios are Poisson with rates 2 and 3 per month.
Their MGFs multiply to exp{2(eᵗ−1)}exp{3(eᵗ−1)}=exp{5(eᵗ−1)}, the MGF of Poisson(5).
The cumulant functions add; every cumulant of the total is 5.
This avoids a convolution and works at every cumulant order.
scenario.q: Why are cumulants easier for independent sums?
scenario.answer: The log-MGF turns products into sums, so cumulants add.

ask.q: Which operation converts products of independent MGFs into addition?
ask.nudge: It is the operation that turns multiplication into addition.

blocks.body: M_X(t)=E(e^{tX}). If finite on an open interval containing zero, derivatives at zero give raw moments and the MGF uniquely determines the law. The lognormal has no finite MGF for positive t.
M'(0)=E(X), M''(0)=E(X²), M'''(0)=E(X³). These are moments about zero, not about the mean.
For independent X,Y, M_{X+Y}=M_XM_Y. For aX+b, M_{aX+b}(t)=e^{bt}M_X(at).
K(t)=log M(t); κ_r=K^(r)(0). For independent sums, K_{X+Y}=K_X+K_Y, so cumulants add.
κ₁=μ; κ₂=σ²; κ₃=μ₃; κ₄=μ₄−3σ⁴. Thus μ₄=κ₄+3κ₂².
Poisson(λ): K=λ(eᵗ−1), every cumulant λ. Binomial(n,p): κ₃=np(1−p)(1−2p). Exponential(rate λ): M(t)=λ/(λ−t), t<λ.

flow.title: From MGF to central moments
flow.note: For independent sums use cumulants; for direct raw moments differentiate M.

ask.q: Why must the MGF exist near zero?
ask.nudge: The derivatives and uniqueness result require finite exponential moments around zero.

scenes.title: Worked example — Poisson cumulants
scenes.problem: Let X~Poisson(3). Find its first four cumulants, mean, variance and third central moment.

steps.why: Every derivative of eᵗ at zero equals one.
The fourth central moment is κ₄+3κ₂²=30.

scenes.after: The fourth central moment is κ₄+3κ₂², not κ₄.

ask.q: What is the fourth central moment of Poisson(3)?

items.a: log M(t), the cumulant generating function.

scenes.objective: Fill the first three binomial cumulants.
scenes.problem: For Binomial(n,p), complete the first three cumulants.

blank.hint: It equals the third central moment.

scenes.after: The third cumulant vanishes for the symmetric binomial case p=1/2.

blocks.body: For Y=aX+b: κ₁(Y)=aκ₁(X)+b; κ_r(Y)=aʳκ_r(X) for r≥2.
For a normal law K(t)=μt+σ²t²/2. Thus κ₁=μ, κ₂=σ² and every cumulant of order r≥3 is zero.

ask.q: Why is κ₄=0 for a normal law although μ₄ is positive?

scenes.title: On your own — exponential cumulants
scenes.problem: For X~Exponential(rate 2), find M(t), E(X), Var(X), κ₃ and μ₃.

scenario.teaser: A student mistakes the second raw moment for the variance.
scenario.title: Raw, central and cumulant quantities differ
body: At fourth order μ₄ and κ₄ also differ: μ₄=κ₄+3σ⁴.
Label every result: raw moment, central moment or cumulant.
scenario.q: For N(2,3), what is M''(0) and the variance?

items.why: False: M''(0)=E(X²), while variance subtracts μ².

items.claim: An MGF must exist near zero for the usual uniqueness result.
items.why: True: existence around zero is the standard MGF condition.

items.claim: Independent MGFs multiply; cumulant functions add.
items.why: True: independence makes MGFs multiply and K add.

items.claim: For aX+b, κ_r=aʳκ_r(X) for r≥2; translation changes only κ₁.
items.why: True: translation affects κ₁ only; higher cumulants scale by powers of a.

items.claim: The lognormal has no finite MGF for positive t.
items.why: True: the lognormal has no finite positive exponential moment.

scenes.title: Transfer problem — binomial cumulants
scenes.problem: For X~Binomial(5,0.2), find M(t), mean, variance and third cumulant.
scenes.check: The third cumulant contains the factor (1−2p).

solution.why: The first two cumulants are mean and variance.
The third cumulant equals the third central moment.

items.q: What is the third binomial cumulant?
Does every distribution have an MGF?
items.a: No; the lognormal has no finite MGF for positive t.
